title: Trump Attends Dignified Transfer of Four U.S. Soldiers Killed in Iran War
excerpt: The ceremony at Dover Air Force Base came as the U.S. death toll in Iran rose to 18, with growing bipartisan opposition and surging oil prices threatening India's energy security.
body:
• President Trump attended the dignified transfer of four U.S. service members killed in Iranian attacks in Jordan and Iraq, bringing the total American death toll to 18.
  • Trump threatened to bomb Iranian bridges and power plants for every ship attacked in the Strait of Hormuz, escalating the five-month-old conflict that Congress has not authorized.
  • The war has cost $37.5 billion so far, with the Pentagon requesting an additional $70 billion in supplemental funding to replenish depleted missile supplies.
  • India's crude oil import bill surged 60% in the April-June quarter due to Strait of Hormuz disruptions, forcing a rapid pivot to Russian and Latin American crude.

President Donald Trump saluted four flag-draped caskets at Dover Air Force Base on Wednesday as the remains of U.S. service members killed in Iranian attacks were returned to American soil, a solemn ceremony that underscored the mounting human cost of a war that shows no signs of ending.

Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth stood at attention as an honor guard carried the caskets from a military cargo plane into transport vehicles. A family member's wail pierced the quiet as one coffin was moved from the aircraft.

"We're going to honor them. For me it's one of the hardest things to do as a president. But it has to be done," Trump told reporters before departing for the ceremony, according to Reuters. Asked what he would tell the grieving families, he said: "All I'm going to say is, we love you. We love your child."

The Fallen

Three of the four soldiers were killed on July 17 when an Iranian missile struck their sleeping barracks at Muwaffaq Salti Air Base in Jordan. They were First Lieutenant Tyler James Feehan, 25, of Ewa Beach, Hawaii; Private Isabella Gonzales, 19, of Carrollton, Texas; and Sergeant Angel S. Rampersad, 28, of Ozone Park, New York. All three were assigned to U.S. Army air defense brigades.

Rampersad had initially been listed as missing after the attack. The Pentagon updated her status to "Duty Status–Whereabouts Unknown" before confirming on Tuesday that she is believed to be deceased. The incident remains under investigation.

"Sgt. Rampersad lived a life of courage and selflessness. New York, and our nation, are safer because of brave Americans like her who answer the call to serve."

— Kathy Hochul, Governor of New York

The fourth soldier, Sergeant Michael Emmanuel Swinton, 30, of Fayetteville, North Carolina, was killed separately on Sunday during a controlled detonation of a downed Iranian drone at Erbil Air Base in northern Iraq.

Escalation on Multiple Fronts

The ceremony came just minutes after Trump posted a new threat on Truth Social, warning that for every ship Iran attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, the United States would "bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT, including those located next to, or in, the Capital City of Tehran."

The United States has now struck Iran for 11 consecutive nights, targeting military command centers, maritime capabilities, missile launch sites, and air defense systems, according to U.S. Central Command. Explosions have been reported near the cities of Shiraz, Konarak, Chabahar, and Abdanan. Iranian officials said 50 civilians have been killed and 500 wounded in the recent U.S. strikes.

The war, launched in February as a joint U.S.-Israeli operation, has cost American taxpayers at least $37.5 billion. Defense Secretary Hegseth told senators this week that the Pentagon needs an additional $70 billion in supplemental funds, in part to replenish depleted missile supplies. Congress has not authorized the conflict.

More than 100 U.S. service members have been injured since July 7 alone, the Pentagon said, though 96% have returned to duty with what were described as minor concussions.

Growing Political Opposition

Public support for the war continues to erode. A Reuters/Ipsos poll conducted this month found that four in five Americans expect the conflict to drag on for an extended period, while only 37% approve of U.S. military strikes against Iran. Leading Republicans, including House Speaker Mike Johnson, have urged a quick resolution.

Trump's approval rating has hovered near the lowest levels of his political career since the conflict began. Republican strategists have warned that rising living costs, fueled in part by higher gas prices, have neutralized the political benefits of his tax cuts ahead of November's midterm elections.

Oil Shock Hits India Hard

The war's economic fallout extends well beyond American borders. India, the world's third-largest oil importer, saw its crude oil import bill surge 60% in the April-June quarter compared with the same period last year, according to India's petroleum ministry data.

With the Strait of Hormuz effectively shut down — through which roughly 40% of India's crude imports and 60% of its LNG imports normally transit — Indian refiners have scrambled to diversify. Middle East oil imports fell 27% to 1.55 million barrels per day between April and June, while imports from Russia surged to a record 2.64 million barrels per day in June, accounting for half of India's total crude intake, according to Reuters.

The disruption deepened this week when Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis threatened to blockade the Bab el-Mandeb Strait in the Red Sea, the main alternate route for Saudi crude bound for Asia. On Tuesday, tankers carrying Saudi oil destined for India and China made U-turns in the Red Sea, heading for the longer Suez Canal route instead.

"There is a growing dependency on imports, and with that comes a vulnerability to geopolitics. I think we are in a geopolitical flux; I think this is going to remain with us for decades, definitely years."

— Vandana Hari, Founder of Vanda Insight, at a Bloomberg event in Singapore

Brent crude hovered above $91 a barrel on Tuesday, with U.S. gasoline prices back above $4 a gallon. The Reserve Bank of India's inflation target of 4% was already breached in June, with consumer prices rising 4.38% year-over-year. Energy analysts warn that the dual chokepoint crisis — Hormuz plus Bab el-Mandeb — could keep prices elevated for months.

What's Next

After the dignified transfer, Trump flew to Marietta, Georgia, offering a ride on Air Force One to Feehan's family, who are from the state. He was scheduled to give remarks on newly activated "Trump accounts" for newborns.

The war's trajectory remains deeply uncertain. Trump has renewed threats to strike Iran's nuclear facility at Natanz, while Iran has promised retaliation. For Indian policymakers and the diaspora watching from the U.S., the twin pressures of a widening conflict and an energy crisis driven by chokepoint closures show no sign of easing.
